axes.model_access:
Each vendor's LM connects uniformly through dspy.LM (OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini/local vLLM etc.,
following the official docs' LM-integration line, not enumerated item by item); its differentiator is **treating prompts as programmable parameters** —
signatures declare inputs and outputs, and optimizers automatically tune prompts and few-shot examples.
axes.runtime:
A Python library (pip-installed into your process); GitHub 38,850★, last push 2026-10-29 (API verified).
Academic origin (Stanford NLP), with industrial-side Databricks investment (per the official narrative).
axes.local_files: The library form runs inside your process; optimization artifacts (program state/examples) land at paths you specify — data never leaves your side.
axes.background: A library has no resident semantics; optimization (teleprompting) is an offline batch task that ends when it finishes.
axes.tools: ReAct-style agent modules and tool calling are within the official module family; MCP support status has no verified official mainline statement.
axes.context: State management follows your program; cross-session memory is not part of its narrative — its "memory" is the optimized examples and weights.
axes.permissions:
No account system; the permission surface is whatever vendors' API keys you connect. The optimization process calls models heavily (a token-cost surface);
budget-control parameters are in the official docs line, details not verified item by item.
axes.fit:
Fits: turning "prompt tuning" into a reproducible optimization process (with metrics, with a training set); pipelines where models are swappable.
Does not fit: wanting an out-of-the-box agent runtime; small samples without metrics (optimizers consume metrics — without metrics there is nothing to optimize).
